parole.significato: A small fruit, usually red, black or yellow, with a smooth hard seed and a short hard stem.

parole.significato: To work on a farm, especially in the growing and harvesting of crops.
parole.testo: From Middle English fermen, from Anglo-Norman fermer (“to let out for a fixed payment, lease, rent”) ultimately from the same Old English source as Etymology 1. Compare Old English feormian (“to feed, supply with food, sustain”).

parole.significato: Comprising greatly varied elements, to the point of incongruity.
parole.testo: From Middle English motle, from Anglo-Norman motteley (“parti-colored”), from Old English mot (“speck”). Doublet of mote. The English word can be analysed as mottle + -y.
From Salop (an abbreviation of Anglo-Norman Salopesberia, from Old English Scrobbesbyrig (“Shropshire”)) + -ian.
